speaker: gm
text:
Wendell Prout turns slowly from the sack hoist above the shut loft door. A pigeon watches from the beam. Below him, a scrawny boy in enormous black boots lobs gutter stones at the body. “Cob says, keep spinning, Mister Prout. Makes a better show.” On the wall, a sharp-faced girl in a shawl swears at the yard in Common, then switches to dock cant for emphasis.

A woman in a rain cape steps away from the gate, notebook open. “Sergeant Agnes Kell. The Captain calls it suicide. I don’t.” Her pencil pauses over the page. A stone clangs off the hoist hook.

speaker: player
text: *I stride into the yard, cape flapping, and plant my fists on my hips.* Fear not, citizens! Sir Bartholomew Puddle, Knight of the Realm, is here! Sergeant, I have already solved it. Clearly the pigeon did it. Look at its shifty little eyes.

speaker: gm
text:
Kell gives the pigeon a brief, dry look. “Noted. The pigeon is not under arrest.” She turns back to her notebook and the yard.

The boy under the body snorts. “Pigeon’s got more sense than a knight, then.” A stone taps against the cobbles.

From the wall, the girl in the shawl swings her heels. “Shifty eyes? Look in a mirror, tin-plume.” Kell’s pencil moves to the open satchel by the gate.

marks.note: You announced that you’d solved the case by blaming the pigeon, so Cob is mocking your certainty.
You called the pigeon’s eyes shifty; the girl turns your insult back on you and mocks your knightly finery.

speaker: player
text: *I wag a gauntleted finger at the boy.* You there, young squire! Cease pelting the deceased at once, it is most unchivalrous. And who, pray, is this Cob who gives such ghoulish orders? Bring him before me!

speaker: gm
text:
Cob catches your gauntleted finger with a suspicious squint. “Cob’s right here, tin-plume. And he don’t take orders from a finger.” He stops throwing stones, but keeps the others clenched in his fist.

Kell’s pencil taps once against her notebook. “Cob is the boy beneath the body, investigator. He answers to Cob.” She looks to him. “No more stones.”

Cob lowers his fist a little. The girl on the wall gives a sharp laugh. “Hear that, Cob? Knight’s brought you up before his court. Mind your manners.”

marks.note: You wagged a finger at him and ordered him to stop; Cob objects to being ordered about that way.

speaker: player
text: Ah! Cob speaks of himself in the third person, as befits nobility. I respect that. Sir Bartholomew respects that. *I turn to Kell and lower my voice to a carrying stage whisper.* Sergeant, what's in the satchel? Evidence? Biscuits? A knight must know.

speaker: gm
text:
The satchel gapes beside you, its empty leather mouth pointed at the cobbles. Kell glances down at it. “Empty. The porters found it that way.” She writes in her notebook, then reads back the entry. “Satchel: open. Contents: none.”

Across the yard, Cob gives a solemn nod. “Nobility’s got a lot of rules. Cob’s got boots.” The girl on the wall snorts, heels drumming the bricks.

speaker: player
text: Boots! Fine boots indeed, Master Cob. Far too big for you. *I squint at them, then at the hanging man's feet.* By my oath... did you steal those boots off Mister Prout? Speak truly before a knight of the realm!

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s mouth shuts. His fists tighten around the stones. “Found ’em.”

The girl on the wall stops drumming her heels. Kell’s eyes move from the too-large boots to the body above the loft door. “The boots fit the deceased’s feet, investigator. Not this boy’s.” Her pencil touches the page. “Boots: worn by Cob. Their ownership disputed.”

Cob scowls at her. “Cob said found ’em.” One boot shifts on the cobbles; its laces are tied in a rough loop around his ankle.

speaker: player
text: *I kneel solemnly before Cob, armour clanking, so we are eye to eye.* Master Cob, a knight does not punish a finder. A knight REWARDS a finder. Tell Sir Bartholomew exactly where you found them, and I shall give you a whole silver piece. *I hold out a coin with great ceremony.*

speaker: gm
text:
Cob eyes the silver in your hand, then your face. He keeps his boots planted firmly on the cobbles.

“A whole silver piece to say where Cob found ’em? That’s not enough to look at ’em, tin-plume. Boots cost extra. Cob’s not cheap.”

He holds out a dirty hand for the coin, but doesn’t move to untie a lace. On the wall, the girl’s heels stop drumming. Kell’s pencil waits above her notebook.

marks.note: You offered Cob a silver piece for telling you where he found the boots, and he wants more before he’ll let you look at them.

speaker: player
text: Haggling! The noble art! Very well. *I press one silver crown into his hand, then dramatically add a second.* Two crowns. That is my entire fortune, Master Cob, save for some shillings and a quantity of pennies. Now: where did you find the boots?

speaker: gm
text:
Cob takes both crowns and closes his fist around them. He glances at the boots, then back at you.

“Two crowns, and you want to know where Cob found ’em? In the yard, obviously. Now it’s three crowns to look. Boots stay on.”

Kell makes a short entry in her notebook. “Payment: two crowns. Question: where the boots were found. Answer: in the yard.” Cob tucks the silver away, his oversized boots still laced fast around his ankles.

marks.note: You paid two crowns for where Cob found the boots; now he wants three more before letting you look at them.

speaker: player
text: *I rise slowly, clanking, and turn my noble profile towards the girl on the wall.* Fair maiden of the battlements! You have the look of one who sees all from on high. I ask you, as a knight who has just been robbed by a child: did you see who strung up poor Mister Prout?

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to find out whether you saw who strung up Mister Prout: 11 + 4 = 15 vs DC 18: failure

speaker: gm
text:
The girl’s heels stop drumming. She looks you over, then points at the loft door.

“I saw him jump. Right out of that door, at midnight. Wailing about his debts. Clear as day.”

Cob barks from across the yard. “That’s what she said!”

Kell writes without looking up. “Witness claims the deceased jumped from the loft door. Noted.” Her pencil pauses. “You’ll want more than a knightly title for the record, investigator.”

speaker: player
text: Debts! Wailing! Midnight! Case closed, Sergeant, the maiden has spoken. *I pause.* Although... the loft door is shut. Did he shut it behind him on the way out? Very tidy fellow, clerks. I shall go up and re-enact the leap for the record. *I march to the granary door to find the stairs to the loft.*

speaker: gm
text:
The granary’s back doors are padlocked, their iron fastened against the wood. There is no stair to be had from this side. Kell watches you reach them, pencil poised.

“Locked. The warden has the key.”

From the wall, the girl gives a sharp, humorless laugh. “He’ll leap up there next, shall he? Saves the trouble of opening a door.”

Kell’s pencil scratches once. “The witness says the deceased jumped from the loft door. That door is barred on the inside.” She looks back to you. “Noted.”

speaker: player
text: Barred on the inside! Then he leapt and the door CLOSED ITSELF in shame. Or a ghost barred it. Stand aside, Sergeant, a knight climbs! *I seize the hoist rope in full chain mail and attempt to haul myself up to inspect Mister Prout and that door.*

speaker: dice
text: Athletics check to climb the hoist rope and inspect Mister Prout and the loft door: 13 + 5 = 18 vs DC 16: success

speaker: gm
text:
Chain mail clanks against the granary wall as you haul yourself up. The rope bows, the hoist beam groans, and you reach it beside Prout, with the loft door close enough to examine.

The door is shut, its bar set on the inside. Prout’s neck bears a second mark: narrow and level beneath the slanting burn of the noose. There’s a swelling beneath the hair at the back of his head. His palms are clean.

From below, Kell calls up, pencil still in hand. “I can’t swear to what you see from here, investigator. Tell me what you find.”

speaker: player
text: *Dangling heroically, I bellow down.* Sergeant! He has TWO neck marks! One slanty, one flat! Clearly he hanged himself twice, the first attempt being unsatisfactory! Also a great lump on the back of his head, where I expect he bumped it on the way up. And his hands are spotless. A very clean clerk. Write all that down!

speaker: gm
text:
Kell writes, her eyes still on the notebook. “Noted. Two marks at the neck. Swelling at the back of the head. Palms clean. Reported by the investigator from the hoist.”

She looks up at you. “That is not a second hanging, investigator.”

Below, Cob has gone very quiet. The girl on the wall watches him instead of you. Kell turns a page in her notebook. “The body needs to come down before I can examine it myself.”

speaker: player
text: Then down he comes, with dignity! *Clinging on with one arm, I draw my longsword and saw through the rope above Mister Prout, while trying to catch him with the other arm so he doesn't fall on young Cob.*

speaker: dice
text: Athletics check to cut the rope and catch Mister Prout without dropping him on Cob: 2 + 5 = 7 vs DC 16: failure

speaker: gm
text:
Your sword saws through the rope. Prout’s weight wrenches free of your grasp and hits the cobbles hard beside Cob.

Cob jerks back, his stones scattering across the yard. The girl on the wall drops down to the yard with a sharp cry. Kell is already moving; she kneels by the body and checks his neck, the back of his head, then his hands.

“Mister Prout…”

Kell’s pencil rests against her notebook. “Two neck marks. A blow to the back of the head. Clean palms.” She looks up at you. “I can sign this as murder.”

speaker: player
text: Murder! Just as I suspected all along, after the pigeon. *I slide down the rope, land in a clattering heap, and rise with enormous dignity.* Ahem. Fair maiden. You said he leapt from a door barred on the inside. Either you are a liar, or a wizard. Which is it? Sir Bartholomew is not angry. Sir Bartholomew is merely very, very disappointed.

speaker: gm
text:
The girl goes flat and still. Her gaze flicks to the body on the cobbles, then back to you.

“I lied. I didn’t see him jump. A gentleman paid me to say it.” She closes her fist tighter around something. “He had a silver-topped cane.”

Kell’s pencil stops. “Witness retracts her claim. Says she was paid.” She looks at the girl. “You’ll have to say that again when it’s entered.”

The girl’s face hardens. “Not to your book.” She drops from the wall and moves close to Cob, putting herself between him and the watch.

marks.note: She’s asking the girl to repeat her retraction for the official record, not denying what she said.

speaker: player
text: A silver-topped cane! The mark of a villain, or a dandy, or both! *I strike a thinking pose.* Fear not, maiden, no book. Only Sir Bartholomew's memory, which is famously... *I pause*...somewhat present. What was his face like? And what are you clutching in that fist, hm? Is it his payment?

speaker: gm
text:
The girl in the shawl glances at your face, then at the body. Her fist opens: a silver crown, stamped with a little wheat-ear.

“His face? Didn’t get a good look. Good coat, silver cane, and enough lavender water to drown in.”

Kell’s pencil moves. “A gentleman paid the witness to lie. Description: good coat, silver-topped cane, strong lavender scent. Payment: one silver crown.” She looks up at the girl. “I’ll record the payment. Not your name.”

speaker: player
text: A wheat-ear on a crown! Treason! Or farming! *I turn sharply to Cob.* Master Cob, show me the crowns I gave you, for comparison. And then tell me truly, now that the maiden has confessed: did the lavender gentleman give you those boots as well?

speaker: dice
text: Persuasion check to have Cob show you the crowns you gave him and tell you whether the gentleman gave him the boots: 8 + 4 = 12 vs DC 15: failure

speaker: gm
text:
Cob’s fist closes over the crowns. He turns his back on you and edges toward the water butt.

“Cob told you. Found ’em. Quit asking.”

The girl in the shawl steps closer to him, between Cob and the watch. Kell writes in her notebook. “Cob declined to show the coins or answer further.” Her pencil lifts. “Boots: still worn. Ownership disputed.”
